**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

The agreement contains no liquidated damages, penalties, or minimum fees payable by Sparkling (our side):

- **Section 11 (Fees)** — Sparkling pays only the Fee Schedule amounts; there is no late-payment interest, penalty, or stipulated-sum mechanic.
- **Section 17(b) (Termination)** — we hold an unqualified right to terminate for convenience on 90 days' notice with **no early-termination fee** and no obligation to pay remaining contract value; our only exit obligations are to cease use and certify return/destruction.
- **Sections 8(b) and 17(c)** — money flows run in our favour on rejection or Garman default (return of amounts paid; conversion to a perpetual, fee-free licence).
- **Section 19 (Non-solicitation)** — mutual, with no liquidated fee for breach.
- The only reference to "penalties" (p0090) sits inside **Garman's indemnity of Sparkling**, which benefits us and is therefore not flagged.

This meets the rule's preferred position (no Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalties), so the fallback 3-month cap is unnecessary. One watch item for the deal team, not a redline under this rule: the Fee Schedule itself was not in the reviewed text, so it is worth confirming it carries no late-payment interest or termination charge that would reintroduce a Customer-payable penalty.
